sources.title: Mobile connectivity you can count on — publication page
facts: Ofcom published the discussion-paper page on 3 June 2026 and requested responses by 29 July 2026.
The page says reliable mobile connectivity requires coordinated action by industry, government, local authorities, landlords and others.
The page lists the discussion paper, qualitative consumer research, Greater Manchester research and train measurement evidence as separate supporting documents.

sources.title: Connectivity you can count on
facts: The discussion paper proposes assessing good mobile performance using download speed, upload speed and latency together.
It proposes a benchmark where good performance is available at least nine out of ten times rather than treating signal presence alone as sufficient.
The document separates policy ambition and crowdsourced performance evidence from exact premises-level service availability.

sources.title: Consumer experiences and understanding of mobile network quality
sources.lines: official supporting-document listing at HTML lines 148-150
facts: Ofcom lists this as qualitative consumer research published alongside the mobile-connectivity discussion paper.
The research was commissioned to explore understanding and experience of mobile-network quality and how quality information could be communicated.
Qualitative findings are evidence about consumer experience and must not be promoted to measured coverage or parcel truth.

sources.title: Beyond Coverage — Mobile Connectivity in Greater Manchester
sources.lines: official supporting-document listing at HTML lines 151-155
facts: Ofcom lists a dedicated Greater Manchester connectivity report published with the discussion paper.
The study examines outdoor, indoor and transport-route connectivity in selected Greater Manchester locations.
The study geography and measurement campaign must remain explicit and cannot be generalised to all UK premises.

sources.title: Beyond Coverage — Mobile Connectivity in Greater Manchester annex
sources.lines: official supporting-document listing at HTML lines 151-155
facts: Ofcom published a separate annex supporting the Greater Manchester connectivity report.
The annex is methodological and evidential support for the bounded measurement study.
Annex material does not establish current orderability at an address or UPRN.

sources.title: Connectivity on Trains Measurement Study
facts: The study measured mobile and onboard Wi-Fi performance across 50 journeys on 24 rail lines during February and March 2026.
Good Performance required at least 5 Mbit/s download, 1.5 Mbit/s upload and latency no worse than 50 milliseconds in the same test cycle.
The report states that route, time, rolling stock and single-day fieldwork limitations mean results are indicative rather than universal.

sources.title: Line by Line Analysis Annex — Connectivity on Trains Measurement Study
sources.lines: official document listing at HTML lines 156-166
facts: Ofcom lists a separate line-by-line analysis annex for the train study.
The annex preserves route-level detail rather than treating the national summary as uniform.
Route-level measurement evidence is not a substitute for a current parcel or provider orderability check.

sources.title: Annex — Pass rates by Segment
sources.lines: official XLSX listing at HTML lines 160-164
facts: Ofcom published segment-level pass-rate data as a separate spreadsheet.
The spreadsheet is an analytical annex to the bounded 2026 train measurement campaign.
Segment pass rates must retain route, operator, test threshold and fieldwork-date context.

sources.title: Annex — Classification by Segment
sources.lines: official XLSX listing at HTML lines 162-165
facts: Ofcom published segment-level failure classifications as a separate spreadsheet.
The classifications support analysis of weak signal, absent signal and other performance constraints.
Classification outputs are campaign evidence and not deterministic predictions for every passenger or premises.

sources.title: Annex — Streetwave Ofcom Rail Data Collection Schedule
sources.lines: official XLSX listing at HTML lines 164-166
facts: Ofcom published the rail data-collection schedule as a separate annex.
The schedule documents when and where the measurement campaign was conducted.
Collection schedules provide lineage and sampling context rather than service-availability evidence.

sources.title: Signal struggles on trains widespread, Ofcom research finds
facts: Ofcom reported that good-performance pass rates across measured train segments varied substantially by operator.
The news page defines good performance using download, upload and latency thresholds together.
It distinguishes the Streetwave rail study, Greater Manchester study and qualitative consumer research.

sources.title: Mobile Matters
facts: Ofcom's Mobile Matters index groups annual crowdsourced mobile-experience reports and supporting datasets.
The 2025 report analyses data collected between October 2024 and March 2025.
The index separates annual reports, chart data and interactive reports.

sources.title: Mobile Matters 2025: using crowdsourced data to assess people’s experience of using mobile networks
facts: The 2025 report covers cellular technology, data connection success, file-transfer times, latency and speed distributions.
The source is crowdsourced device-performance evidence rather than a census of all locations.
Results are analysed by mobile network operator and location and therefore require method and period metadata.

sources.title: Mobile Matters 2025 — Chart data
facts: Ofcom lists chart data separately from the Mobile Matters 2025 narrative report.
The chart data supports reproducibility of published aggregate findings.
Chart aggregates must not be converted into exact address-level mobile availability.

sources.title: Mobile Matters Interactive report 2025
facts: Ofcom published an interactive presentation of the 2025 Mobile Matters analysis.
The interactive is another presentation layer for the same bounded crowdsourced evidence.
It must not be double-counted as an independent measurement campaign.

sources.title: Mobile Matters 2024 report
facts: Ofcom preserves the 2024 Mobile Matters report in the annual report index.
The report is a prior-vintage crowdsourced mobile-experience source.
Trend use requires keeping 2024 and 2025 collection periods and methods distinct.
